headline_marked: [[12 Questions]] to Ask Before Buying a Text-to-SQL Tool
headline: 12 Questions to Ask Before Buying a Text-to-SQL Tool
summary: Don't let your AI data tool quietly produce wrong numbers. Learn the critical questions to ensure accuracy, access control, and compliance before you buy.
details: Text-to-SQL tools demo beautifully, generating charts from natural language queries in seconds. However, the demo is the easy part. The real test comes with production databases, complex schemas, and month-end reporting.

Accuracy is a major concern. While models are good at writing plausible SQL for small, clean schemas, performance drops sharply on real-world databases with hundreds of tables and cryptic column names. The industry benchmark BIRD exists because academic results don't survive contact with production data.

Vendors often claim high accuracy based on model class (e.g., GPT-class) or lack of complaints. However, these are not measurements. True validation requires testing against your own schema and asking specific questions you know the answers to.

Beyond accuracy, access control is critical. Ensure the tool enforces permissions at the database level (row-level security) rather than just filtering results in the application layer. A query running against everything and then being filtered afterwards poses a significant security risk.

Ambiguity in business terms (e.g., 'revenue' can mean gross, net, booked, or shipped) is a failure mode that prompts can't fix. Without a defined semantic layer, different users asking the same metric in different ways can get different numbers, eroding trust.

Look for tools that clearly distinguish between a query executing successfully and one that matches a known-correct result. Features like verification badges or confidence indicators often only mean the query ran without error, not that the answer is true.

To test accuracy, ask 10 questions you know the answers to in a single session and count the results. Also, test for distinct counts and how the tool handles ambiguous phrasing by asking for the same metric in multiple ways.
caption:
AI can write SQL, but can it be trusted?

headline_marked: [[Linux From Scratch]] project offers custom Linux builds from source
headline: Linux From Scratch project offers custom Linux builds from source
summary: Build your own Linux system from the ground up with LFS, providing step-by-step instructions for compiling every component from source code.
details: Linux From Scratch (LFS) is a project that guides users through the process of building a custom Linux operating system entirely from source code. This approach offers unparalleled control and understanding of the system's components.

The LFS project is maintained by a dedicated organization that oversees its development and provides comprehensive documentation. It currently consists of several subprojects, each contributing to the overall ecosystem.

By compiling software from source, users can optimize their systems for specific hardware and needs, potentially achieving better performance and a smaller footprint compared to pre-compiled distributions.

The project has been active since 1998, with ongoing development and updates to ensure compatibility with the latest software and technologies. The website design is credited to Jeremy Huntwork and Matthew Burgess.
